summary: The S. 539 PROTECT Our Children Reauthorization Act of 2025 reauthorizes and updates federal programs focused on preventing and investigating the online exploitation of children. Specifically, it extends the National Strategy for Child Exploitation Prevention and Interdiction and the Internet Crimes Against Children (ICAC) Task Force Program through fiscal year 2028, provides increased funding levels, updates reporting requirements, and grants certain legal liabilities protections to ICAC task forces regarding their lead prioritization decisions.

affected_groups.effect: Task forces and participating agencies receive reauthorized grant funding, clearer directives to identify child victims, broader cooperation frameworks, and limited liability protections for lead prioritization decisions.
affected_groups.group: Federal, State, Local, Tribal, and Military Law Enforcement Agencies

affected_groups.effect: Staff gain liability protections from federal and state lawsuits stemming from case prioritization choices, barring instances of intentional misconduct or gross negligence.
affected_groups.group: ICAC Task Force Personnel and Participating Officers

affected_groups.effect: The DOJ must update the National Strategy for Child Exploitation Prevention and Interdiction every four years instead of every two years, incorporating streamlined threat assessments and resource estimates.
affected_groups.group: The Department of Justice and Federal Agencies

key_provisions: Reauthorizes and updates the National Strategy for Child Exploitation Prevention and Interdiction, changing its update frequency from every two years to every four years and streamlining its required components.

Reauthorizes the Internet Crimes Against Children (ICAC) Task Force Program and explicitly authorizes specific funding amounts for fiscal years 2026 ($70 million), 2027 ($80 million), and 2028 ($90 million).

Provides limited liability for ICAC task forces, participating law enforcement agencies, and their personnel against civil claims or criminal charges arising from decisions to prioritize specific internet crime leads, excepting intentional misconduct, actual malice, or gross negligence.

Expands the duties of ICAC task forces to explicitly include identifying child victims, prioritizing investigations likely to rescue children, and educating the judiciary regarding technology-facilitated crimes and offender characteristics.
Requires the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children to provide all supplemental data along with reports of online sexual exploitation to law enforcement agencies.
missing_information: The full text of the original 2008 act being amended is not provided in the source material, only specific amendments.
Specific details on how the grant funds will be divided among individual states or local task forces beyond broad percentage mandates.

Specifically, it extends the National Strategy for Child Exploitation Prevention and Interdiction and the Internet Crimes Against Children (ICAC) Task Force Program through fiscal year 2028, provides increased funding levels, updates reporting requirements, and grants certain legal liabilities protections to ICAC task forces regarding their lead prioritization decisions.
summary_detail.significance: This bill significantly impacts the operational framework, funding, and legal liabilities of federal, state, and local law enforcement networks dedicated to combating the online sexual exploitation of children through fiscal year 2028.
